story_type: warship fire at the pier, helicopter bucket drops and tugs fight it for four days
hook: A Navy warship burned for four days at the pier.
narration: A Navy warship burned for four days, tied to a pier in San Diego.
The fire aboard USS Bonhomme Richard was called away on the morning of July 12, 2020, while the ship was in maintenance.
Navy helicopters carried buckets of water over the ship, again and again.
[short pause] Three helicopter squadrons made more than fifteen hundred water bucket drops.
Tugs sprayed the hull from the waterline. Cooling the steel slows the heat moving through the ship.
On the pier, firefighters climbed scaffolding up the side of the ship.
outcome: After four days of firefighting, all known fires aboard were out, and no one was hospitalized.
title: Warship burned for 4 days at the pier
description:
A fire broke out aboard the amphibious assault ship USS Bonhomme Richard on July 12, 2020, while it was moored pier side at Naval Base San Diego for maintenance. Navy helicopter squadrons made more than 1,500 water bucket drops, tugs cooled the hull, and after four days all known fires were extinguished.

Footage: U.S. Navy video by Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Jessica Paulauskas, Commander, Naval Surface Force, U.S. Pacific Fleet, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/759806/sailors-and-federal-san-diego-firefighters-fight-fire-aboard-uss-bonhomme-richard
